name: Gomer (Hosea's wife)
title: The Unfaithful Wife as a Symbol of Israel
summary: Gomer was the daughter of Diblaim and was called by God to become the prophet Hosea's wife. She was an unfaithful woman whose marriage to Hosea became a living picture of God's relationship with unfaithful Israel. Her story illustrates both Israel's spiritual adultery and God's unconditional love and willingness to reconcile.

keyEvents.title: The Marriage with Hosea
keyEvents.description: God commanded Hosea to take an unfaithful wife to illustrate Israel's adultery against the Lord. Hosea took Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, as his wife.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Jezreel
keyEvents.description: Gomer gave birth to her first son, who was named Jezreel, a prophetic name that foretold judgment on the house of Jehu for the bloodshed in the Valley of Jezreel.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Lo-Ruhama
keyEvents.description: Gomer gave birth to a daughter who was named Lo-Ruhama, meaning 'no mercy,' as a sign that God would no longer show mercy to the house of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Lo-Ammi
keyEvents.description: The third child, a son, was named Lo-Ammi, meaning 'not my people,' as a symbol that Israel had broken the covenant with God.

keyEvents.title: Hosea Buys Back Gomer
keyEvents.description: After Gomer left Hosea to live in unfaithfulness, the prophet was commanded to love her again and buy her back. This symbolized God's endless love for Israel.
